statement: Massport's 2022 Environmental Status and Planning Report (ESPR) used a 10- to 15-year future planning horizon of 53.5 million annual passengers and 495,000 aircraft operations for Logan. Massport reported that 2024 passengers were about 19% below that level and 2024 operations about 16% below.
assumptions: Single-year planning scenario 10 to 15 years after the 2022 ESPR; 495,000 annual aircraft operations in the same scenario.
limitations: A planning-horizon scenario rather than a year-by-year forecast; it does not compare demand with terminal capacity.
source_title: Boston Logan International Airport 2023/2024 Environmental Data Report, Chapter 3: Activity Levels
source_locator: Section 3.1.5 and Figure 3-11, pp. 3-21 to 3-22

statement: Phase 1 of the Terminal E Modernization added four gates, which opened in October 2023. Phase 2, which proposed three more gates and a direct pedestrian connection to the Blue Line Airport Station, remained deferred as of the end of 2024.
limitations: Reports project status as of the end of 2024; does not state terminal capacity in passengers.
source_title: Boston Logan International Airport 2023/2024 Environmental Data Report, Chapter 4: Airport Planning
source_locator: Section 4.2.2 Terminal E Modernization, pp. 4-10 to 4-11

statement: The Bradley International Airport Master Plan Update forecast passenger enplanements to grow from 3.21 million in 2017 to 4.65 million by 2037 and airline operations from 67,500 to 87,700.
assumptions: Base year 2017 with 3.21 million enplanements; 20-year master plan forecast.
limitations: Executive summary dated March 2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic.
source_title: Bradley International Airport Master Plan Update: Executive Summary (March 2019)
source_locator: Forecast of Aviation Demand (PDF page 5)

statement: The Master Plan Update's facility requirements called for additional aircraft gates and more capacity for security screening, baggage screening, hold rooms, concessions and integrated Federal Inspection Services. The recommended concept expands Terminal A in the short term and ultimately builds a new Terminal B as an extension of Terminal A.
limitations: The executive summary does not quantify the number of additional gates.
source_title: Bradley International Airport Master Plan Update: Executive Summary (March 2019)
source_locator: Facility Requirements and Development Concepts (PDF page 6)

statement: In January 2026 the Connecticut Airport Authority completed a new concourse extending Terminal A with three additional airline gates. It is part of an 80,000-square-foot facility that also houses an inline baggage screening system opened in fall 2025; the two terminal projects cost about $250 million.
limitations: Passenger use was expected within weeks of the January 23, 2026 announcement; the release does not state terminal capacity in passengers.
source_title: Bradley International Airport Caps Off Terminal Expansion with Unveiling of Newly Constructed Concourse
source_locator: News release

statement: The PVD Master Plan, approved by the FAA in 2021, projects annual enplanements rising from 1,969,966 in 2017 to 2,553,530 at Planning Activity Level (PAL) 1, 2,997,929 at PAL 2 and 3,715,999 at PAL 3.
assumptions: Base year 2017; forecast levels are tied to Planning Activity Levels rather than calendar years, and projects are implemented as activity reaches each level.
limitations: RIAC states that COVID-19 reduced activity and pushed master plan projects to later years.
source_title: Rhode Island T.F. Green International Airport Master Plan: Executive Summary
source_locator: Approved Forecasts of Aviation Demand (PDF page 3)

statement: The master plan's facility requirements found that PVD will need 32 aircraft gates (35 narrow-body equivalent gates) by the end of the planning period (PAL 3), compared with 22 existing positions. Existing hold rooms are well below acceptable levels in peak periods and should double in area by PAL 1.
assumptions: Average utilization of 2.5 daily departures per gate on the peak-month average day; the plan notes that a different operating model or gate utilization could change the requirement significantly.
limitations: The inventory section of the same plan lists 21 aircraft parking positions, while Table 5.16 shows 22 existing positions.
source_title: PVD Master Plan Report, Section 5: Facility Requirements
source_locator: Table 5.16 (PDF page 29); hold room requirements and Table 5.21 (PDF page 35)

statement: The master plan proposes Project T1-1 (PAL 1), a two-level expansion of about 21,000 square feet at the end of the south concourse allowing two more wide-body and two more narrow-body gates, and Project T2-1 (PAL 2), a pier concourse of about 137,000 square feet with four additional wide-body and five additional narrow-body gates.
assumptions: Timing is tied to Planning Activity Levels rather than calendar years.
limitations: Concept renderings are preliminary; the summary gives no construction schedule.
source_title: Rhode Island T.F. Green International Airport Master Plan: Executive Summary
source_locator: Project T1-1 (PDF page 5); Project T2-1 (PDF page 6)

statement: The Jetport's Sustainable Airport Master Plan forecast passenger enplanements growing from 843,944 in its base year to 1,010,139 in 2025 and 1,187,969 in 2035, with airline passenger activity growing about 1.5% a year.
assumptions: Based on the 2013 FAA Terminal Area Forecast; the plan departed from the TAF only in its operations forecasts.
limitations: Older plan; the summary exhibit does not label the base year. The Jetport later reported record traffic in 2024 and 2025 (see pwm-record-traffic-2025).
source_title: Portland International Jetport Sustainable Airport Master Plan: Executive Summary
source_locator: Exhibit 6 Forecast Summary, Executive Summary p. 22 (PDF page 24)

statement: The Jetport reported a record 2,593,067 passengers in 2025, above the previous record of 2,438,054 set in 2024, and said it was the first New England airport to surpass pre-pandemic levels, in 2023.
limitations: Annual traffic count; does not by itself measure unmet demand.
source_title: Portland International Jetport: Jetport Sets All-Time Record for Passenger Traffic in 2025
source_locator: News release

statement: In July 2025 the Jetport opened a $21.6 million, 4,200-square-foot addition to the passenger concourse with three new passenger boarding bridges, which it describes as part of its strategy to maintain customer experience while traffic sets records.
limitations: The release does not state whether gate count or terminal capacity changed.
source_title: Portland International Jetport: Jetport Sets All-Time Record for Passenger Traffic in 2025
source_locator: News release, section Expanded Passenger Amenities Added in 2025

statement: Project NexT, a terminal expansion that added new gate areas, jet bridges and vendor space and modernized baggage claim and airline support areas, opened to screened passengers in March 2026. The airport says the added capacity positions it to attract and sustain additional air service.
limitations: The release does not state the number of gates or a passenger capacity.
source_title: Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport: Leahy BTV Celebrates Opening of Project NexT
source_locator: News release

statement: BTV lists an upcoming South Terminal Replacement that will replace the aging South Concourse with a modern terminal addition featuring expanded gate areas, improved passenger amenities and enhanced circulation space.
limitations: The page gives no size, gate count, schedule or demand rationale.
project_status: Upcoming (listed among current airport improvement projects)
source_title: Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport: Airport Improvement
source_locator: Current Projects, South Terminal Replacement

statement: The Master Plan Update identifies long-term terminal items (such as a new ticket lobby vestibule, an expanded bag claim area and direct concourse access to bag claim) as needed when annual enplanements reach Planning Activity Level 2 of 2.25 million; its short-term terminal items focus on optimizing and renovating existing space. The plan records a historical peak of 2.1 million enplanements in 2005.
assumptions: 2009 base year with about 1.5 million enplanements; forecast of 1.9 to 2.3 million enplanements in 2020 and 2.3 to 2.8 million in 2030.
limitations: Older plan whose forecast was not realized; MHT reported over 1.38 million total passengers (arriving and departing) in 2025 (see mht-traffic-2025).
source_title: Manchester-Boston Regional Airport Master Plan Update: Executive Summary
source_locator: Section 2.1 Passenger Enplanements (PDF page 7); Section 4.4 Long-Term Terminal Planning (PAL 2), p. 13 (PDF page 17)

statement: MHT reported that over 1.38 million passengers flew in and out of the airport in 2025, an increase of almost 9% over 2024 and its best year since 2019.
limitations: The release gives a rounded lower bound rather than an exact count.
source_title: Manchester-Boston Regional Airport: Record-Breaking Cargo Volumes and Strong Passenger Growth Drive MHT's Best Year Since the Pandemic
source_locator: News release

statement: An FAA Airport Terminal Program award (FY2026, $10,000,000) partially funds construction of a new 81,568-square-foot terminal at Tweed-New Haven, which the FAA list says will add four gates, increase passenger screening areas and include a new baggage handling system to accommodate increased demand.
limitations: The FAA's 2023 FONSI/ROD describes the replacement East Terminal as having four gates and two additional boarding positions, with a net increase of one terminal gate (see hvn-fonsi-2023-operations).
project_status: Planned; FAA FY2026 Airport Terminal Program selection
source_title: FAA FY2026 Airport Terminal Program Selections (May 18, 2026)
source_locator: Connecticut, New Haven (HVN), page 2 of 12

statement: The FAA's environmental decision for the runway extension (to 6,575 feet) and a replacement East Terminal of about 80,000 square feet with four gates and two additional boarding positions expects 9,928 air carrier and air taxi operations in 2026 and 16,352 in 2031 with the project, compared with 5,560 in 2022. Total terminal gates increase by one.
unit: air carrier and air taxi operations
activity_direction: aircraft operations (air carrier and air taxi)
assumptions: Proposed Action scenario; the FAA states that the additional gate will accommodate existing and forecast operations and passengers at an acceptable level of service.
limitations: Some terminal elements are outside the FAA's airport layout plan approval authority under the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018.
project_status: FAA Finding of No Significant Impact and Record of Decision signed December 21, 2023
source_title: FAA Finding of No Significant Impact and Record of Decision: Tweed-New Haven Airport Runway 02-20 Extension and Terminal Expansion
source_locator: Section II, Proposed Action, pp. 4-5

statement: In July 2026 the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit upheld the FAA's environmental review for the East Terminal project and left the FONSI in place. The project still requires Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection approval and review by the East Haven Planning and Zoning Commission.
limitations: Status statement from the airport; no construction schedule is given.
project_status: Federal approval in place; state and local approvals pending
source_title: Tweed-New Haven Airport: Court Upholds FAA Review and HVN Project Moves Forward
source_locator: News release

statement: Bangor International Airport's $14.2 million project connects the domestic and international terminals after security to provide much-needed additional gate space. The airport cited passenger growth of more than 30% over five years and high demand for more space and amenities after security.
limitations: The release planned about 18 months of construction starting in April 2024. BGR's Ticket to a Better BGR project page, checked on 2026-10-23, describes construction of the connector and a Gate 6 waiting-area expansion; completion was not verified.
source_title: Bangor International Airport: Passenger and Facility Improvements Scheduled for BGR
source_locator: News release

statement: An FAA Airport Terminal Program award (FY2026, $2,180,000) partially funds rehabilitation and expansion of Martha's Vineyard Airport's passenger terminal, including hold rooms, security screening checkpoints and airline ticketing, to accommodate increased demand.
limitations: The FAA list gives no size, gate count or schedule.
project_status: FAA FY2026 Airport Terminal Program selection
source_title: FAA FY2026 Airport Terminal Program Selections (May 18, 2026)
source_locator: Massachusetts, Vineyard Haven (MVY), page 5 of 12

statement: LAX served about 73.71 million passengers in 2025, 3.76% fewer than in 2024. Departing load factors were 84.28% on domestic and 81.40% on international flights, and commercial aircraft operations fell 0.13% to 580,996.
limitations: Single-year change; not a forecast.
source_title: LAX Specific Plan Aviation Activity Analysis Report CY 2025
source_locator: Section B, Summary and Conclusions, p. 2

statement: LAWA's Airfield and Terminal Modernization Project includes a new Concourse 0 as an eastward extension of Terminal 1 (up to 1.275 million square feet) and a new Terminal 9 (up to 1.4 million square feet); the new facilities would replace 15 of the West Remote Gates that a Taxiway D extension would remove or the project would decommission.
limitations: The page does not state net gate additions, a schedule or passenger capacity.
source_title: LAWA: Airfield & Terminal Modernization Project Elements
source_locator: Project elements page

statement: The amended 1985 Settlement Agreement limits John Wayne Airport to 12.2 million annual passengers from 2026 through 2030, or 12.5 million if 11.21 million passengers were served in 2021-2025 and specified mitigation measures are met, and limits passenger service to 95 Class A average daily departures through 2030. The passenger limit was 11.8 million in 2021-2025.
limitations: Which of the two Phase 3 limits applies depends on conditions the page does not resolve.
source_title: John Wayne Airport: Key Provisions of Settlement Agreement
source_locator: Key provisions table, rows Term, Average Daily Departures and Million Annual Passengers

statement: John Wayne Airport served 11,369,865 passengers in 2025, up 2.5% from 11,089,405 in 2024.
limitations: Served traffic is constrained by the Settlement Agreement passenger limit (11.8 million annual passengers through 2025), so it may understate unconstrained demand.
source_title: John Wayne Airport Posts December 2025 Statistics
source_locator: News release, year-to-date table

statement: San Francisco Planning's 2019 notice for the SFO Recommended Airport Development Plan states that long-term demand is forecast to reach 71.1 million annual passengers, the estimated maximum capacity of the existing airfield, and that the plan proposes no airfield project that would increase that capacity. SFO served about 57.8 million passengers in 2018.
assumptions: Landrum & Brown aviation activity forecast of April 2014, approved by the FAA on June 9, 2014; about 25% of passengers connect at SFO.
limitations: 2019 planning document; later environmental review and approval status of the plan was not checked.
source_title: San Francisco Planning: Notice of Preparation of an EIR, SFO Recommended Airport Development Plan (Case No. 2017-007468ENV)
source_locator: Project Summary, pp. 1-2; Project Location, p. 4

statement: The plan's proposed Boarding Area H would add domestic and international swing gates for 8 wide-body or 13 narrow-body aircraft, with one international gate lost at Boarding Area G. The notice states that SFO is currently deficient in gates and handles some scheduled flights at remote hard stands with passenger busing.
limitations: The plan would not increase airfield capacity, so passenger growth stays bounded by the estimated 71.1 million annual passenger airfield capacity (see sfo-radp-airfield-capacity).
source_title: San Francisco Planning: Notice of Preparation of an EIR, SFO Recommended Airport Development Plan (Case No. 2017-007468ENV)
source_locator: Project description, item (1) Boarding Area H, p. 5

statement: The FAA's 2019 capacity profile reports SFO hourly capacity of 104-107 operations in visual conditions and 93-98 in marginal conditions with side-by-side arrivals on runways 28L and 28R, and 71-78 in instrument conditions, when arrivals to the closely spaced parallel runways are in trail.
assumptions: Each range spans the ATC facility-reported rate and the model estimate; the visual and marginal figures are for the 28/01 side-by-side configuration and the instrument range covers the two in-trail configurations.
limitations: The FAA states that the profile does not consider non-runway constraints and does not replace detailed analysis for investment decisions.
source_title: FAA Airport Capacity Profile: San Francisco International Airport (2019)
source_locator: Overview and weather definitions, pp. 2-3; visual, marginal and instrument configurations, pp. 4-14

statement: An FAA briefing on SFO's simultaneous offset instrument approach procedures notes that runways 28L and 28R are separated by 750 feet centerline to centerline.
limitations: Older procedure briefing; only the runway geometry is cited, not current approach procedures.
source_title: FAA presentation: SFO Simultaneous Offset Instrument Approach (SOIA) RNAV (GPS) PRM
source_locator: PDF page 9

statement: The FAA-approved 2023 forecast for the ANC Master Plan projects total enplaned passengers rising from 2,564,262 in FY2022 to 4,056,254 in FY2042, a compound annual growth rate of 2.3%.
assumptions: Base year FY2022; the FAA approved the forecast on August 30, 2023 as consistent with the Terminal Area Forecast.
limitations: The FAA approval letter states that approval does not justify future projects and that actual activity must reach planning activity levels.
source_title: Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport Master Plan: Forecast of Aviation Demand
source_locator: Chapter 3, Table 3-13 Total Enplaned Passengers (PDF page 36)

statement: The 2026 ANC Airport Master Plan finds that expanding the South Terminal and increasing use of the North Terminal is necessary to meet future passenger demand: 1 to 3 additional or improved gates and near-term ticketing, security screening and baggage make-up capacity at PAL 1, and 8 additional gates by PAL 3. It recommends expanding the A and B Concourses (Phase 1) and extending the C Concourse to connect to the North Terminal (Phase 2).
assumptions: Requirements are tied to Planning Activity Levels derived from the master plan forecast.
limitations: Executive summary figures; detailed requirement tables are in the plan chapters.
source_title: Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport 2026 Airport Master Plan: Executive Summary
source_locator: Terminal Facility Requirements (PDF page 7); Passenger Terminal phasing (PDF page 10)
